page: The Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-24 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine configuration built for artificial intelligence inference, graphics rendering, and multimedia workloads. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz, paired with 96 GB of system memory. Hardware acceleration is provided by two NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPUs, supplying a combined 48 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached disk options for non-volatile data persistence.

Benchmark results highlight an operational divergence between general CPU compute and GPU acceleration tasks. Single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core scoring at 1059.0 and stress-ng single-core processing, fall into the bottom 25% of tested systems. Multi-threaded host processing and memory throughput operate within the middle 50% tier, showing 102.71 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 18,984.81 on stress-ng multi-core. In contrast, the dual NVIDIA L4 GPUs achieve top-tier performance for LLM inference, reaching 11,848.39 tokens/sec for small model prompt processing and 2,725.09 tokens/sec for 7B parameter model prompt processing, both positioning in the top 10% tier.

The hardware configuration provides high resource efficiency for inference pipelines where full-size data center accelerators like the A100 or H100 are unnecessary. Because host single-core compute is modest and local storage is absent, the machine is not designed for storage-heavy databases or compute-bound serial compilation tasks. Instead, the balance of 48 GB VRAM, 96 GB RAM, and dedicated hardware media engines makes the g2-standard-24 suitable for multi-stream video transcoding, medium-scale LLM model hosting, computer vision inference, and cloud workstation rendering.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-24 is an accelerator-focused instance configured with 24 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs, 96 GB of RAM, and two NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPUs providing 48 GB of total VRAM. The instance contains no bundled local storage. While CPU benchmarks show modest single-thread performance placing in the lower quartile, multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth rank in the middle 50%. The primary strength of the instance lies in machine learning inference, where prompt processing and generation benchmarks for small to medium language models reach the top 10% to 25% of cloud systems. This architecture offers solid density and cost efficiency for GPU-accelerated workloads, making it well-suited for medium-scale generative AI inference, computer vision processing, and virtualized graphics rendering without requiring oversized enterprise accelerators.
